clue.text: Minister takes tea, no milk, no sugar

blocks.note: cha is an old slang word for tea
tea served with nothing added is plain

explanation.surface: A vicar asks for a cup of tea served black and unsweetened.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman attached to a college, hospital or regiment is a kind of church minister.

clue.text: The chair might include one toilet break

blocks.note: the head is a ship's toilet, a naval term
a break from work is a rest

explanation.surface: A committee chair schedules a pause so everyone can visit the lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The chair' suggests a person chairing a meeting; here it is simply a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Many seats, such as car or dentist seats, have a cushioned support for the back of the head built in.

clue.text: Old gym buddy with special rates

indicators.note: a special arrangement is an unusual one, so the following word's letters are set out differently

blocks.note: a buddy is a pal
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old training partner from the gym offers a discounted membership.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece the palaestra was a public school for wrestling and athletics, a gymnasium of antiquity.

clue.text: A match with no start gun, bats or breathing gear

indicators.note: having no start means the opening letter of the word for match is dropped
bats is slang for crazy, so the letters of gun go haywire

blocks.note: taken as written
to match something is to equal it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A list of sports kit: match equipment without a starting pistol, cricket bats or diving gear.
explanation.walkthrough: EQUAL loses its E to leave QUAL; the surface reads 'bats' as cricket bats, but it is the anagram signal for gun.
explanation.definitionFit: An aqualung is the portable apparatus divers wear to breathe underwater, so it is gear for breathing.

clue.text: Out of bounds? Birdie after getting past it

indicators.note: after places the bird word behind the phrase that opens the clue

blocks.note: read cryptically: with no bounds or leaps, there is no spring
a birdie, a little bird, here a hen

explanation.surface: A golfer gets a birdie despite a ball going out of bounds, though they are past it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of bounds' and 'Birdie' both suggest golf; the question mark flags that 'out of bounds' must be read as having no leaps left.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone no spring chicken is an idiom for saying they are no longer young, which is ageing.

clue.text: Taco filling used in desert sweetmeat

indicators.note: the filling of a taco is what sits inside, so only its inner letters are kept
something used in another thing is placed inside it

blocks.note: to maroon someone is to desert them on an island
the two central letters of taco

explanation.surface: A Mexican taco's stuffing is used in a sweet treat served in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like a misspelt dessert or a sandy place, but it is the verb meaning abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaroon is a small almond or coconut biscuit, an old-fashioned confection called a sweetmeat.

clue.text: Proceeds from a social, around five shillings

indicators.note: around means the social event wraps itself about the numeral

blocks.note: taken as written
a social is a party, such as a dance
V is the Roman numeral five
s was the abbreviation for shillings in old British money

explanation.surface: The takings from a club party came to about five shillings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proceeds' looks like a noun meaning takings; it is the verb meaning moves forward. A shilling was a pre-1971 British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: To proceed is to go forward, and to advance is to move forward, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: It’s plastic lining stone sides of open ditch

indicators.note: plastic material can be moulded into a new form
the sides of a word are its outermost letters
a lining sits inside the things that follow it

blocks.note: jet is a black stone used in jewellery
the letters of it's, without the apostrophe
the first and last letters of open

explanation.surface: Plastic is lining the stone edges of an open drainage channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditch' sits at the end looking like a trench; it is the verb meaning throw away.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison something is to throw it overboard or discard it, just as you ditch unwanted things.

clue.text: Publication to pass on material

blocks.note: an organ is a newspaper or journal that speaks for a group
to pass away is to die

explanation.surface: A magazine article is going to be handed on to someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass on' reads as one phrase meaning hand over; 'pass' alone means die and 'on' is just a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Organdie is a fine, stiff, translucent cotton fabric, a type of cloth.

clue.text: Frequency with which everyone mocks easy victims

blocks.note: f is the standard abbreviation for frequency
everyone is all
to guy someone is to ridicule them

explanation.surface: Some unfortunate people are mocked by everybody, and often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' as a verb meaning tease is mainly British.
explanation.definitionFit: A fall guy is a scapegoat or dupe who takes the blame, so such people are easy targets.

clue.text: Nice game, not hard to get fifty in

indicators.note: not means the letter for hard is taken out of the game word
the game word is made to take in the numeral, so it goes inside
in places the numeral within the shortened game bird

blocks.note: pheasant is a game bird
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
L is the Roman numeral fifty

explanation.surface: A pleasant game that isn't too difficult lets you reach fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the French city, but here it is the plain adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nice is agreeable and enjoyable, which is what pleasant also describes.

clue.text: Sportsman with others regularly skipped algebra

indicators.note: skipping at regular intervals leaves every second letter of the word

blocks.note: w is a common abbreviation for with
the others are the rest
the second, fourth and sixth letters of algebra

explanation.surface: An athlete and his teammates kept missing their maths lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrestler competes in a combat sport of grappling, so he is an athlete.

clue.text: They ask for payment on board expresses

blocks.note: someone on board a ship or train is in it
to voice an opinion is to express it

explanation.surface: Express trains are carrying bills for the passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expresses' suggests fast trains, which fits 'on board'; it is the verb meaning utters.
explanation.definitionFit: An invoice is a bill sent by a supplier that requests settlement of money owed.

clue.text: Goons mixed up with gangster in funny business

indicators.note: things mixed up are jumbled out of their usual order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Thugs have become entangled with a mobster in some shady racket.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes in 'in' as well as the two nouns, which is easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Funny business means odd or suspicious activity, exactly what peculiar happenings are.

clue.text: Quickly shut up about instruments one breaks

indicators.note: about means the hush word goes round the rest
breaks means the numeral splits the instruments word open and sits inside

blocks.note: sh is the order to be quiet
harps are musical instruments
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Somebody is told to be quiet quickly after damaging the band's instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions stack here: the numeral goes in first, then the hush word wraps everything. Sharpish is informal British for promptly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharpish is British slang meaning promptly or without delay, as in 'get here sharpish'.

clue.text: Run over by French comedian riding cycle

blocks.note: r is the cricket abbreviation for run
o is the cricket abbreviation for over
Jacques Tati was a French film comedian
someone riding a horse is on it

explanation.surface: A French comic on a bicycle has been knocked down.
explanation.walkthrough: In the surface a comedian on a bike gets run over; each word is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A cycle is a repeating sequence, and rotation is the turning round in regular order.

clue.text: Rhubarb is not to French taste, perhaps

blocks.note: non is French for not
taste is one example of the five senses

explanation.surface: Rhubarb is a vegetable the French reportedly don't enjoy eating.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhubarb is British slang for nonsense, from actors muttering 'rhubarb' as background chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage, rhubarb means meaningless talk or rubbish, exactly what drivel is.

clue.text: Sort of drink from India, drunk chilled mostly

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the phrase is kept, losing its final letter

blocks.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a sot is a drunkard
a drink chilled is on ice

explanation.surface: A beverage from India is drunk mostly cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' reads as a verb about the drink; it is the noun for a drunkard.
explanation.definitionFit: Isotonic sports drinks have the same salt and sugar concentration as body fluids, a category of beverage.

clue.text: Surmounting obstacle is skinny runner’s challenge

indicators.note: in a down clue, surmounting means sitting on top, so this piece comes first

blocks.note: gaunt means very thin
a let is an old word for a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: Getting over a hurdle is the real test for a thin athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: Running the gauntlet means passing between two lines of attackers, so it is a trial for a runner.
explanation.definitionFit: Running the gauntlet is the ordeal faced by one who must dash between rows of assailants.

clue.text: Plenty whine after going outside

indicators.note: outside means the word for after wraps around the word for whine

blocks.note: once can mean as soon as, as in 'once you leave'
to pule is to whimper or whine

explanation.surface: A dog whines after being let outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is the hard piece: it means 'as soon as', as in 'once you go'. 'going' is only a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulence is great wealth or luxury, an abundance of riches, which is what plenty can mean.

clue.text: Stun somewhat like Bond’s DB5?

blocks.note: James Bond drove an Aston Martin DB5
the suffix -ish means somewhat like

explanation.surface: A stun gun is a bit like the gadgets in Bond's famous car.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that ASTON stands for the whole car by its make.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish someone is to amaze them so greatly that they are left stunned.

clue.text: Hard plays periodically put on under canvas

indicators.note: periodically means at intervals, keeping every other letter
put on means placed after the canvas phrase

blocks.note: someone camping under canvas is in a tent
the second and fourth letters of plays

explanation.surface: Tough dramas are sometimes staged in a marquee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard' is an adverb here, as in 'stare hard'.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking hard at something means looking with fixed concentration and close attention.

clue.text: A tip circulated about the clubs being dismal

indicators.note: circulated means moved around, so these letters change places
about means the rearranged letters surround the next word

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A betting tip spread around the golf clubs proved hopeless.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathetic is used informally to describe something feeble and miserably inadequate.

clue.text: Exciting fish adds variety in the van

indicators.note: in the van means at the front, so this word leads

blocks.note: a variety is a kind
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A thrilling fish brings variety to the delivery van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' reads as a vehicle; 'in the van' is short for in the vanguard.
explanation.definitionFit: To kindle interest or passion is to arouse it, so the participle means stirring up feelings.

clue.text: Rogue whose son makes footwear

indicators.note: rogue means wayward and out of control, so the letters stray

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rascal's boy turns out to be a cobbler.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowshoe is a wide racquet-shaped frame strapped under a boot for walking on soft snow.

clue.text: Couple visiting a French city’s finer points

indicators.note: a visitor goes into a place, so this word goes inside

blocks.note: Nice is a city in southern France, with the possessive s
to couple is to tie together

explanation.surface: A pair of tourists visits Nice and admires its best features.
explanation.definitionFit: Niceties are subtle details or delicate distinctions, the small refinements of a matter.
